result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of sidewalks on both sides of a two-lane road, but they lack consistent buffers and are in fair to poor condition. The absence of marked crossings and the presence of blank frontages and narrow walkways on one side contribute to a low-protection environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Narrow and Unbuffered Sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the right side is narrow and lacks a buffer from traffic, placing pedestrians in close proximity to moving vehicles.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks, which may encourage unsafe mid-block crossing behavior.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Enclosure
hazards.description: The large dumpster enclosure on the left creates a visual barrier that could hide pedestrians from oncoming traffic near the curb cut.

interventions.title: Install High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility paint to provide designated and safer crossing points for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Repair
interventions.description: Widen the narrow sections of the sidewalk and repair cracked surfaces to ensure a continuous, ADA-compliant path.

interventions.title: Add Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Implement a planting strip or street trees to provide a physical separation between the sidewalk and the travel lanes.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with row houses and a narrow sidewalk directly adjacent to the roadway. While a continuous walkway exists, there is no buffer between pedestrians and moving traffic, and parked vehicles create significant visual obstructions.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is immediately adjacent to the travel lane with no planting strip or physical barrier to protect pedestrians from vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the right side of the roadway where the silver car is parked.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parking
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians who may attempt to cross the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and mid-ground where cars are parked along the curb.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the ends of the block to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Incorporate a planting strip or furniture zone to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement vertical traffic calming measures to ensure vehicle speeds remain low in this residential context.

result.summary: The street is a two-lane roadway with sidewalks on both sides, serving a mix of residential row houses and commercial land use. Pedestrian safety is limited by the lack of marked crossings and a large, wide vehicle access point for a supermarket parking lot that creates a significant conflict zone.

hazards.name: Wide Driveway Conflict Zone
hazards.description: The supermarket on the right has a wide, undefined entrance where vehicles can cross the sidewalk at various angles, increasing the risk of pedestrian-vehicle collisions.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, entrance to the supermarket parking lot

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks visible, forcing pedestrians to cross the two-lane road without designated protection or priority.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parallel parked cars on the left side of the street may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

interventions.title: Driveway Narrowing and Definition
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the supermarket entrance and use bollards or curbs to clearly define vehicle paths, reducing the conflict area for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Marked Midblock Crossing with Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to potential crossing points to ensure clear sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a surface parking lot that lacks a dedicated, separated walkway for people accessing the commercial building. Pedestrians must navigate a shared space with maneuvering vehicles, and the pavement is in poor condition with visible cracking and uneven surfaces.

hazards.name: Lack of Separated Walkway
hazards.description: Pedestrians must walk through the active parking lot to reach the store entrance, creating conflict points with vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and middle ground across the entire paved area

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Significant cracking and uneven concrete surfaces create trip hazards for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of Lighting
hazards.description: No pedestrian-scale or street lighting is visible, which reduces safety and security after dark.

interventions.title: Designated Pedestrian Walkway
interventions.description: Install a clearly marked and physically protected walkway (using bollards or a raised curb) to separate pedestrians from the parking area.

interventions.title: Pavement Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair and level the cracked concrete to provide a smooth, accessible walking surface.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lights or building-mounted luminaires to improve visibility for pedestrians at night.
